name: Srisaila Mahakshetram (Srisaila Devasthanam)
address: Srisaila Devasthanam, Srisailam, Nandyal District, Andhra Pradesh
main_deity: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy (2nd Jyotirlinga) and Sri Bhramaramba Devi (6th Maha Shakti Peetha)
other_deities: Saptamatrikalu (Brahmani, Maheshwari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Indrani, Chamundi)
Pancha (Pandava) Lingalu (Yudhishtara Lingam, Bhima Lingam, Arjuna Lingam, Nakula Lingam, Sahadeva Lingam)
description: Srisaila Mahakshetram is considered as Kailasa on Earth. The history and tradition have it that the merits earned by visiting Srisailam are equal to worshipping all the divine powers of the universe. Srisaila Mahakshetram is the living embodiment of ancient and spiritual-cultural traditions and values. Visited by many great saints like Adi Shankaracharya, rulers mainly Sri Krishna Devaraya, Chatrapathi Sivaji and several other spiritual personalities; Srisailam is the supreme repository of spiritual truth. When Goddess Parvati asked Lord Shiva about his most desired place apart from Kailasa in the Universe, he chose Srisailam, the avatar of Sri Chakra. In such a significant location, Shiva-Shakti take the form of Sri Mallikarjuna Bhramaramba to bless all their devotees. Among the 12 Jyotirlingas, the 2nd is Mallikarjuna Swamy Lingam; among the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas, the 6th is Sri Bhramaramba Devi temple. Srisailam is the only temple where two such icons exist under one temple premise.
history: Srisailam has great ancient significance and has been a worshipping place for millions of devotees over thousands of years. Inscriptional evidence starts from South India's first dynasty, the Satavahanas. Satakarni, the third Satavahana king (3rd century C.E.), was an ardent devotee of Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy and named himself Mallanna, mentioning Srisailam as Chakora Shetagiri. Post Satavahanas, the Ikshvaku dynasty considered Srisailam a holy destination. In the 6th century C.E., Kadamba king Mayura Sharma addressed Srisailam as Sriparvatam. Kadamba ruler Bruhaddhana unified Sriparvatam after defeating Pallava rulers. Badami Chalukya ruler Pulakeshi built many temples and was the first Kshatriya to perform Shiva Deeksha. Dantidurga (735-755 C.E.) of Rashtrakuta Empire ruled lands around Sriparvatam. Kalyana Chalukyaraju Trayalokamalya Deva (980-1058 C.E.) established a gopuram on Garbhalayam, and his grandson in 1069 C.E. donated a village for Satrams and Dharamshalas. Rulers of Hoysala dynasty collected crystal Shiva Lingams from Patalaganga near Krishna River and built temples. Prataparudra of Kakatiya dynasty and his wife visited, performed Tulabhaaraseva. 13th century Reddy ruler Prolaya Vema Reddy donated Raamatheertham village, and his son Anavema Reddy laid steps for devotees to reach Patalaganga. Shivaji Maharaj visited, offered prayers, appointed a special army to guard the temple, and built a portrait/sculpture receiving the divine sword from Bhramarambika Devi.
mythology: According to Puranas, Nandi-Parvat took form following the Tapasya of Siladha Maharshi; Parvat became Srisailam (Kailasa on Earth) and Nandi became Lord Shiva's vehicle and head of Ganas. Lord Shiva entered an Arjuna tree entwined with jasmine creeper, becoming Mallikarjuna. Princess Chandravathi offered a pure, never-withering garland of jasmine (Mallika) flowers to Lord Shiva, who tied it around his head and vowed to stay as Mallikarjuna as long as sun and moon exist. Devotee Manjari proved that visiting Srisailam destroys all sins and grants Mukti without rebirth. After destroying Ravana, Sri Rama accompanied by Sita Devi and Lakshmana visited Srisailam on Agastya Maharshi's advice, established Sahasralingam, and performed Sriramapradakshina to cleanse Brahmahatyadosham. The five Pandavas established five Lingams (Yudhishtara, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva) during their visit. Sage Dattatreya performed Tapasya under Triphala Vruksham. Narada cursed Nalakubera and Manigriva to become Arjuna trees, which were uprooted by child Sri Krishna. Saptamatrikalu were sent to stop Andhakasura's blood from touching the ground during Lord Shiva's battle.

sub_temples.name: Sanagala Basavanna
sub_temples.location: In front of Lord Shiva sanctum
sub_temples.significance: Prime devotee and vehicle Nandi representing Dharma; head of all Ganas whose consent is mandatory before worshipping Lord Shiva.

sub_temples.name: Ratnagarbha Ganapathi (Chintamani Ganapathi)
sub_temples.significance: Exclusive Chintamani avatar brought by Shiva-Parvathi

sub_temples.name: Sudarshana Veerabhadra Swamy
sub_temples.significance: First protector deity greeting devotees; swallowed Sudarshan Chakra during Daksha Yagna destruction.

sub_temples.name: Jwala Veerabhadra Swamy
sub_temples.location: Facing North, to the left of 5 Pandava Lingas
sub_temples.significance: 10-armed idol with regional depiction wearing skull garland, created from Shiva's matted locks.

sub_temples.name: Kumara Swamy Shrine
sub_temples.significance: 6-faced, 12-armed deity balancing 6 enemies of mind; dearest son of Shiva-Parvati who inspired their move to Srisailam.

sub_temples.name: Uma Maheswara Swamy Temple
sub_temples.significance: Depicts Ardhanarishwara Tattva with Shiva seated on throne holding Uma on left thigh; site of Parvati's penance.

sub_temples.name: Vruddha Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
sub_temples.location: Facing North to main Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
sub_temples.significance: Ancient temple with decorated inner walls and Dvarabhandhams featuring Gajalakshmi, Lion, and guardians.

sub_temples.name: Rama Prathistitha Sahasra Lingam
sub_temples.significance: Sahasralingam established by Lord Rama to cleanse Brahmahatyadosham after slaying Ravana.

sub_temples.name: Seetha Prathistitha Sahasra Lingam
sub_temples.significance: Sahasralingam consecrated by Sita Devi alongside Lord Rama.

sub_temples.name: Raja Rajeswara & Raja Rajeshwari Temple
sub_temples.location: Northeast of Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple, facing West
sub_temples.significance: Oldest temple complex inside sanctum; Gaja Lakshmi Devi and 4-armed Rajarajeshwari seated on throne.

sub_temples.name: Ardhanareeswara Temple
sub_temples.location: North of Mallikarjuna Temple, facing East
sub_temples.significance: Seated idol in Lotus Pose depicting combined form of Shiva and Parvati with Lion vehicle.

sub_temples.name: Saptamatrikalu Shrine
sub_temples.significance: 7 divine mothers (Brahmani, Maheshwari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Indrani, Chamundi) who stopped Andhakasura's blood.

sub_temples.name: Pancha (Pandava) Lingalu
sub_temples.location: Courtyard of Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple
sub_temples.significance: 5 Lingas established individually by Yudhishtara, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva.

sub_temples.name: Nagula Katta
sub_temples.significance: Subramanya Swamy worshipped in serpent form across 8 serpent demigods to eradicate Nagadosha and Kujadosha.

sub_temples.name: Triphala Vruksham
sub_temples.significance: Combined Medi (Brahma), Raavi (Vishnu), Juvvi (Shiva) tree where Dattatreya & Nrusimha Saraswathi performed Tapasya.

sub_temples.name: Tella Maddi Vruksham
sub_temples.significance: Sacred Arjuna tree representing manifestation of Lord Shiva, Vishnu, and Ganesha.

sub_temples.name: Sami (Jammi) Vruksham
sub_temples.significance: Aparajita Devi in disguise; hiding spot of Pandava weapons worshipped on Vijayadashami.

sub_temples.name: Sri Gokulam (Go Pooja & Gosala)
sub_temples.significance: Houses over 1500 cows providing milk for Abhishekams and Panchagavya by-products.

sub_temples.name: Jagadguru Panditharadhya Peetham
sub_temples.significance: Surya Simhasana Peetham of Veera Saivam tradition led by Dr. Channa Siddharama Panditharadhya Sivacharyulu.

architecture.style: Ancient South Indian Dravidian & Chalukyan stone architecture with intricately carved inner Garbhalayam walls, pillared halls, and decorative doorways.

highlights.name: Vruddha Mallikarjuna Garbhalayam & Dvarabhandhams
highlights.description: Northern facing ancient Garbhalayam with two doors (North and East), decorated inner walls, and Dvarabhandhams featuring two guardians, lotuses, Gajalakshmi, and a Lion.

highlights.name: Rajarajeshwara & Rajarajeshwari Temple Complex
highlights.description: The oldest temple complex at Mallikarjuna Swamy temple, housing Gaja Lakshmi Devi and Rajarajeshwari seated on a throne.

highlights.name: Shri Chakra Layout
highlights.description: Entire temple complex and precinct architecture aligned in the form of Sri Chakra and Bindu-Natha.

highlights.name: Mallika Gundam Structure
highlights.description: Covered water body featuring roofing and 16 stone columns creating multiple hallways, reflecting the topmost part of Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in its water.

highlights.name: Triphala Vruksham & Marble Dattatreya Shrine
highlights.description: Fusion tree of Medi, Raavi, and Juvvi trees with an adjacent marble sculpture of Lord Dattatreya.
